objective: Prepare a secure pilot-first GLPI production rollout in which Microsoft 365 identity is authoritative, existing users can sign in, and managed computers report reliable hardware and software inventory.

in: Assess the current GLPI repository deployment and identity/inventory guidance
Select the correct Entra cloud-only or hybrid AD integration path
Document least-privilege GLPI Agent deployment through Intune or the MSP
Document existing Microsoft 365 user provisioning and sign-in
Add safe configuration scaffolding that contains no tenant secrets
out: Creating tenant credentials without an authorized administrator
Broad endpoint deployment before pilot acceptance
Storing passwords, client secrets, certificates, or tokens in Git

constraints: Microsoft 365 or AD/Entra remains authoritative for identities and groups.
Use a pilot device and pilot user group before broad rollout.
Preserve and test a local GLPI break-glass administrator.
Stop at any credential, admin-consent, or production deployment gate requiring tenant authorization.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Current GLPI deployment assumptions, tenant topology decision, and required roles are documented.
A pilot-first GLPI Agent rollout procedure explains monitor and printer coverage, limitations, packaging, validation, rollback, and broad-deployment gates.
The identity procedure clearly distinguishes cloud-only Entra SCIM/OAuth SSO from hybrid/on-premises LDAP and enables existing Microsoft 365 users without duplicate identities.
Secrets remain outside the repository, least privilege is specified, and local break-glass access is preserved.
Changed repository content passes deterministic checks and independent review.

assessment.reason: The work affects production identity, authentication, endpoint software distribution, and potentially most managed computers.
surfaces: Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Intune
unknowns: Whether the tenant is cloud-only, hybrid, or has reachable AD DS.
Which Entra and Intune roles the user holds.
Whether endpoints are Intune-enrolled or managed solely by the MSP.
The production GLPI URL and external connectivity design.
Whether GLPI SCIM and OAuth SSO plugins are installed and licensed.

practices.practice: Discover topology and privileges before changing production systems.
practices.reason: Entra cloud-only and LDAP/hybrid require different architectures and privileges.

practices.practice: Use pilot-first deployment with explicit validation and rollback.
practices.reason: Inventory agents and sign-in changes affect endpoints and access.

practices.practice: Use least privilege, external secret storage, and break-glass access.
practices.reason: Identity integrations require sensitive credentials and admin consent.

practices.practice: Run deterministic repository checks and independent review.
practices.reason: Operational guidance must be internally consistent before production use.

obligations.text: Assess current deployment, topology questions, and required Entra/Intune/AD privileges.
Provide an actionable pilot-first agent rollout and asset validation procedure.
Provide the correct Entra or LDAP source-of-truth sign-in procedure without repository secrets.
Verify changed content and obtain independent review.

testing.reason: Final verification covers all changed operational guidance.

evidence.summary: Source-bound model self-review of the current-state assessment against the running GLPI 11.0.9 container, empty plugin list, repository deployment documentation, GLPI identity/inventory runbooks, Microsoft Intune RBAC guidance, Microsoft Entra provisioning-role guidance, and GLPI SCIM/OAuth guidance. The assessment correctly separates cloud-only Entra from hybrid AD, states that Entra access alone does not grant Intune deployment rights, preserves break-glass access, avoids secrets, and identifies the production URL and tenant topology as blocking inputs.

evidence.summary: Source-bound model self-review of both identity runbooks against GLPI SCIM and OAuth SSO guidance, Microsoft Entra application provisioning and role documentation, and the inspected GLPI deployment. The guidance correctly rejects LDAP for cloud-only tenants, prevents dual SCIM/LDAP provisioning, separates SCIM lifecycle from OAuth authentication, requires deterministic existing-account reconciliation and pilot scope, avoids invented broad Graph permissions, keeps secrets external, and preserves a local break-glass administrator.

risks.mitigation: Determine cloud-only versus hybrid topology before implementation.

risks.text: A broad agent deployment could expose packaging, proxy, TLS, or duplicate-asset problems.
risks.mitigation: Pilot on a small ring and require inventory acceptance before expansion.

risks.text: An SSO configuration error could lock administrators out.
risks.mitigation: Retain and test the local break-glass account before enabling or enforcing SSO.

risks.text: Secrets or excessive Graph permissions could be exposed.
risks.mitigation: Use external secret storage, least privilege, scoped groups, and documented rotation.
